statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of seven public archetypes. Authenticated play/account management, live multiplayer completion, checkout/donation completion, and destructive account actions were not exercised because they require credentials, another player, payment, or side effects.

page.framework: Server-rendered Lichess UI with progressively enhanced ES modules
page.notes: Public, multilingual, app-like chess service. Homepage and article preserve 95–97% of rendered words without JavaScript.

checkOutcomes.method: screenshot comparison under emulated light and dark preferences
checkOutcomes.evidence: The light and dark captures are byte-identical and both retain the dark palette; the DOM reports html class="dark" rather than a system-driven theme.

checkOutcomes.method: computed animation and stylesheet probe under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
checkOutcomes.evidence: The preference matched, no active animations were returned, and the fetched site stylesheet contains four prefers-reduced-motion rules.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse contrast audit plus prefers-contrast stylesheet probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found 11 low-contrast text/control cases, while the fetched stylesheets contain no prefers-contrast or forced-colors adaptation.

checkOutcomes.method: rendered route/state review and fetched CSS feature probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Home, training, analysis and article surfaces use abrupt document/state changes; fetched CSS contains no @view-transition or view-transition-name usage.

checkOutcomes.method: visual review and fetched CSS probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: No parallax, scrollytelling or scroll-linked animation is present on the representative pages, so there is no main-thread scroll-animation anti-pattern to replace.
The site stylesheet uses overscroll-behavior and the chess/puzzle surfaces use direct board interaction without a competing scroll or pointer-driven page effect.

checkOutcomes.method: long-page screenshots and fetched CSS probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The 2,957 px mobile lobby and 7,501 px mobile tournament listing retain static chrome with no scroll progress/state response; no scroll-state query was found.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM/CSS inspection of menus and dropdown surfaces
checkOutcomes.evidence: Navigation/preferences use fixed/custom dropdown containers; fetched CSS contains no anchor-name, position-anchor or position-try fallback positioning.
Representative navigation uses abrupt page replacement and long listings expose no progress marker, transition cue or destination highlight beyond the current tab underline.
No consent wall, ad interstitial or load-time modal obscured the lobby, puzzle, analysis board, article or login form.
No modal overlay was present on load; the visible disclosure/navigation controls are native buttons, inputs and links and did not block content.
The board and article content dominate their viewports; there are no ads and only compact global chrome.
Lobby and tournament pages both report scrollWidth 360, clientWidth 360 and zero horizontal overflow with a viewport meta tag.

checkOutcomes.method: fetched CSS feature probe across reused components
checkOutcomes.evidence: No @container or container-type rules were found in the three page stylesheets; complex lobby cards, carousels and board sidebars adapt only at page/viewport level.
The login username receives a strong blue focus ring, controls remain operable as buttons/links, and primary mobile actions have generous target sizes.
Quick pairing, puzzle instruction, analysis board, tournament heading, article title and sign-in form each make their purpose and next action apparent.
An anonymous user can select a pairing, solve a loaded puzzle and open the analysis board without registration; sign-in is confined to account-specific activity.
Puzzle state says “Your turn” and identifies the side to move; the 404 clearly says Page not found and links back to the homepage.
Lighthouse measured LCP 3.7 s (outside the good <=2.5 s range), although CLS was 0 and TBT 0 ms; a warm trace measured LCP 1.06 s.
Mobile lobby and tournament observers both report CLS 0 with no shifts; Lighthouse also reports CLS 0.
The trace reports zero long tasks and 0 ms total blocking time; both mobile layout captures also observed no long tasks.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR, DOM and Lighthouse delivery audits
checkOutcomes.evidence: The load transfers about 440 KB with no errors or redirects; scripts are modules/deferred in DOM. Lighthouse estimates only 130 ms render-blocking savings.
The 440 KB load has no tracker bundles and Lighthouse did not report unused or duplicated JavaScript/CSS audits as failures.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility audit and DOM control inventory
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found two unnamed carousel buttons and nine content/flair images without alt; training and analysis probes also enumerate icon-only buttons without accessible names.
Lighthouse reports insufficient contrast for Register, feed timestamps/links and tournament text (11 affected nodes).
The homepage, puzzle, analysis and login rendered with no h1; complex board tools expose many icon-only controls. The login field itself has a clear visible focus ring.

checkOutcomes.method: visual review at desktop and mobile
checkOutcomes.evidence: Body copy, board coordinates, form labels and article text are readable without clipping; mobile layout remains single-column and stable.
The viewport allows user scaling (no maximum-scale/user-scalable=no), and tested mobile pages reflow with zero horizontal overflow. No essential timed media appears on tested paths.
Lighthouse scored Best Practices 1.00 and did not report console errors or uncaught exceptions.
Doctype and UTF-8 are valid, but 9 images lack intrinsic dimensions and 3 are over 2x display size; the load happened to record CLS 0.
Best Practices scored 1.00; BFCache exclusions are WebSocket/no-store constraints, and no permission prompt or paste prevention appeared.
Homepage and article have descriptive unique titles and meta descriptions, all present in raw HTML.
Robots allows crawling and no-JS coverage is 95%, but Lighthouse flags the search trigger implemented as an <a> with no href as non-crawlable.
Both homepage and sampled article return 200 and robots allows them, with extensive hreflang on home, but neither exposes rel=canonical and robots.txt declares no Sitemap URL.
The article has accurate Open Graph title, description, URL, type and image, but has no JSON-LD or microdata for its Article entity.

checkOutcomes.method: headers, cookies, secrets and DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, X-Frame-Options DENY, secure HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie and a nonce-based meta CSP are present; secret scan found none.
No known trackers were found; external traffic is confined to Lichess-owned asset/image/socket origins and no third-party cookies were set.
No permission prompt occurred on load, but the public sign-in UI exposes password plus one-time code only and no passkey/WebAuthn option.
HSTS, X-Frame-Options and Permissions-Policy are present, but response CSP, X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy are absent; the meta CSP cannot provide all header-only protections.
Raw HTML preserves 95% of homepage and 97% of article content; neither page is a JS shell.
Lobby, puzzle, analysis and listing loaded into stable, usable states without cut-off overlays or fragile blank shells.
A complete standalone web app manifest with 32–1024 px icons is linked and a service worker registration controls the lichess.org scope.
An invalid route renders a clear 404/Page not found state and a direct homepage recovery link rather than a blank shell.
The document declares en-US and exposes hreflang variants including Arabic and Persian; language-specific routes are server-rendered.
Live dates and times use semantic <time datetime=UTC> values with localized display strings (for example “in 12 hours” and localized titles).
Event timestamps are stored as unambiguous Z/UTC datetime values and localized for display with explicit UTC context.
The service is ad-free, exposes Donate rather than disguised sponsorship, and presents sign-in/register choices without consent nags or forced continuity.
Sign-in fields use labels and required constraints, password reset is visible, and the failure route provides a clear recovery action.
Username, current password and authentication code use autocomplete=username, current-password and one-time-code respectively.
The sampled sign-in screen clearly separates Sign in/Register, offers password reset and does not obscure pricing or introduce a subscription commitment.

checkOutcomes.method: image primitive and Lighthouse image-delivery audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: All sampled raster content uses WebP, but 18 below-fold images omit lazy loading, 9 omit srcset, 3 are oversized and Lighthouse estimates 18 KiB savings.
The trace records no long tasks/TBT, the 440 KB load has no repeated errors or redirects, and no tracker-driven background work was detected.
The initial page transfers about 440 KB, has no autoplay media and no known trackers; asset traffic is hosted on Lichess-owned domains.
Agent-facing WebMCP tools and on-device inference are emerging and not required for this public chess experience; crawler-readable content is evaluated separately under discoverability.

checkOutcomes.method: heap snapshots and in-page metrics across 10 and 50 preference-menu cycles
checkOutcomes.evidence: A one-time preferences load raised snapshot size from 6.43 MB to 6.69 MB; 50 cycles remained bounded at 6.57 MB. The 10-cycle in-page probe grew only 640 bytes and 22 DOM nodes.
The interactive lobby snapshot remains about 6.4–6.7 MB self size with roughly 104k–111k heap nodes, proportionate to a live chess lobby.
Growth plateaus between 10 and 50 repeated menu cycles rather than scaling with cycle count; the menu closes and DOM count remains near baseline.

paths.description: Public lobby and primary play entry point; covers global navigation, pairing controls, live content, theme, responsive layout and load behavior.
Anonymous puzzle journey; represents the primary interactive learning/game task.
Long-lived analysis-board application; represents a complex interactive tool and memory-sensitive session.
Dense listing/index archetype; covers navigation, responsive reflow and live data presentation.
Long-form article archetype; covers content legibility, crawler rendering and rich/share metadata.
Authentication form; covers labels, autofill, focus and account-flow posture.

findings.evidence: Emulated light and dark screenshots are byte-identical and both show the dark theme; html is hard-coded class="dark" for a fresh profile.
findings.suggestedFix: Use color-scheme: light dark and initialize the default theme from prefers-color-scheme, while preserving an explicit saved user override.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences have no dedicated adaptation
findings.evidence: No prefers-contrast/forced-colors rule was found and Lighthouse identified 11 existing contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast styles for essential text/controls, avoid suppressing system colors, and test the affected registration/feed/tournament states.

findings.summary: Route and state changes are abrupt
findings.evidence: Fetched CSS has no View Transition declarations across representative lobby, board and article navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-document board/panel changes and eligible cross-document navigation with View Transitions, respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-state guidance
findings.evidence: The mobile lobby is 2,957 px and tournament listing 7,501 px tall, while chrome stays static and no scroll-state query/progress affordance is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or scroll-state-responsive header on long listing/content templates, with a no-motion presentation under reduced motion.

findings.summary: Custom dropdown positioning does not use anchors
findings.evidence: Navigation/preferences dropdowns are custom/fixed and the fetched CSS has no anchor-name, position-anchor or position-try.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning with position-try fallbacks for eligible menus/tooltips, retaining a conventional positioned fallback for older browsers.

findings.evidence: Across abrupt route changes and very long listings there is no transition, destination highlight or progress cue beyond a current-tab underline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add focused destination highlighting or directional transitions to high-value route and in-page changes without adding decorative motion.

findings.summary: Complex reused components rely only on viewport layout
findings.evidence: No @container/container-type rules occur in the fetched page CSS despite cards, carousels and side panels appearing at materially different widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reused lobby cards, board sidebars and article/list modules where their available container, not the viewport, determines layout.

findings.summary: Cold-load LCP misses the good threshold
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 3.7 s, while the direct trace measured 1.06 s; the variance still establishes at least one tested cold-load condition outside the <=2.5 s good range.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the Lighthouse LCP candidate, preserve early discoverability/fetch priority, and reduce the short render-blocking chain; validate under throttled repeat runs.

findings.summary: Primary interactive surfaces contain unnamed controls
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found unnamed carousel buttons and nine images without alt; puzzle and analysis probes enumerate multiple icon-only buttons with no accessible name.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon-only control an aria-label or visible name; use empty alt for decorative images and meaningful alt where images convey content. Verify the board accessibility tree and blind mode.

findings.summary: Several text and control colors fail WCAG contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identifies Register, feed timestamps/links and tournament text among 11 low-contrast nodes.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust theme tokens so normal text reaches 4.5:1 and large/UI text reaches the applicable minimum in every theme and contrast mode.

findings.summary: Key app pages lack a clear top-level heading and expose weak control structure
findings.evidence: Home, puzzle, analysis and login render no h1, and complex board probes include many unnamed icon controls; this weakens orientation even though visible field focus is strong.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a programmatic h1/page name (visually hidden where necessary), preserve logical landmarks, and complete names/focus semantics for board controls.

findings.summary: Image markup omits sizing and responsive-delivery hints
findings.evidence: The image primitive reports 9 images without dimensions, 9 without srcset and 3 over twice their display width.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio and responsive srcset/sizes; keep decorative flair dimensions explicit to prevent future shifts.

findings.summary: The search affordance is an href-less anchor
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags header #clinput a.link because it is an <a> without href, making it non-crawlable and semantically misleading.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a button for opening search, or provide a real href to a search page if it is navigation.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap signals are incomplete
findings.evidence: Neither the homepage nor sampled article exposes rel=canonical, and robots.txt contains no Sitemap declaration despite public localized content.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit a self-referencing canonical on indexable templates and declare the canonical sitemap URL in robots.txt; keep hreflang/canonical clusters consistent.

findings.evidence: The sampled article has accurate Open Graph fields but no JSON-LD or microdata describing the Article entity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add schema.org BlogPosting/Article JSON-LD matching the visible headline, author, dates, canonical URL and image.

findings.summary: Several response-level browser defenses are missing
findings.evidence: The main response lacks CSP, X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy headers. A nonce-based CSP exists only as meta; HSTS, X-Frame-Options and Permissions-Policy are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Move/duplicate CSP into the HTTP response (including frame-ancestors), add X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and an explicit strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter Referrer-Policy.

findings.summary: Public authentication offers passwords but no passkey path
findings.evidence: The login form exposes username, current-password and one-time-code fields, with no visible or probed WebAuthn/passkey option.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration and authentication as a phishing-resistant option, retaining password recovery during migration and requesting credentials only in user-initiated context.

findings.summary: Below-fold images are not deferred or responsively selected
findings.evidence: All 18 sampled images are below fold without lazy loading, 9 lack srcset, 3 are oversized, and Lighthouse estimates 18 KiB potential savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold editorial/feed imagery and provide srcset/sizes; retain eager/high priority only for the true LCP asset.
